text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet lifted price controls on 15 basic foods in line with pledges to the International Monetary Fund to liberalise trade, Trade minister Valentin Vassilev said.
-- Bulgaria's government cut import tax on meat by 50 percent to $400 per tonne in a move to boost competition on the domestic market, Trade minister Valentin Vassilev said. @
-- Danone-Serdika, the Bulgarian subsidiary of France's dairy producer Danone said it had raised its capital by $4 million to $15 million.
-- Bulgaria's Interior ministry said it would tighten control on car registration in the country from next month to crack down on car thefts.
-- Seven big foreign firms have bid to advise Bulgaria on the sale of its state carrier Balkan Airlines so far, Privatisation Agency executive director Alexander Sabotinov said.
-- Czech's Unionbank is interested in buying a 51 percent stake in Bulgaria's private Trakiabank, Trakiabank's executive director Emil Simeonov said.
-- Sunflower oil seeds producers proposed an export tax of $100 per tonne to prevent a possible consumption gap after the new harvest. @
-- A World Bank mission arrived in Sofia to discuss country's grain trade policy after the Trade ministry proposed on Monday a 15 percent export fee on wheat exports.
The World Bank has earmarked loans of up to $290 million for Bulgaria this year.
-- Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov, who left for a three-day official visit to Kuwait, said he hoped to secure some $100 million loan from Kuwait to support reforms in Bulgaria. @
-- Bulgaria's cabinet ordered an audit of the country's biggest state refinery Neftochim which posted a loss of 33.4 billion levs last year, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.

-- Bulgaria's government scrapped minimum prices for domestic bad debt bonds known as ZUNKs as part of preparations to introduce a currency board system from July 1, Finance minister Muravei Radev said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
